questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Center and Radius of a Circle by Completing the Square
questions.problem: Find the center and radius of the circle whose equation is ${x}^{2}+2x+2y+{y}^{2}+1=0.$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the center and radius of the circle, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares.

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+2x+2y+{y}^{2}+1 & =0 \\ ({x}^{2}+2x)+({y}^{2}+2y) & =-1 \\ ({x}^{2}+2\cdot x+{1}^{2})+({y}^{2}+2\cdot y+{1}^{2}) & =-1+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2} \\ ({x}^{2}+2\cdot x+{1}^{2})+({y}^{2}+2\cdot y+{1}^{2}) & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can factor the perfect squares and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+1)^{2}+(y+1)^{2} & ={1}^{2} \\ (x-(-1))^{2}+(y-(-1))^{2} & ={1}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the circle is centered at $(-1,-1)$ and its radius is $1.$

questions.problem:
Find the radius and center of the circle whose equation is
$2{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}-8x+8y+3=0.$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the center and radius of the circle, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares.

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}-8x+8y+3 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-4x+4y & =-\frac{3}{2} \\ ({x}^{2}-4x)+({y}^{2}+4y) & =-\frac{3}{2} \\ ({x}^{2}-2\cdot 2x+{2}^{2})+({y}^{2}+2\cdot 2y+{2}^{2}) & =-\frac{3}{2}+{2}^{2}+{2}^{2} \\ ({x}^{2}-2\cdot 2x+4)+({y}^{2}+2\cdot 2x+4) & =\frac{13}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can factor the perfect square and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-2)^{2}+{(y+2)}^{2} & =\frac{13}{2} \\ (x-2)^{2}+{(y-(-2))}^{2} & ={(\sqrt{\frac{13}{2}})}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the circle is centered at $(2,-2)$ and its radius is $\sqrt{\frac{13}{2}}.$

questions.problem:
Find the radius and center of the circle whose equation is
${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+5x-3y-8=0.$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the center and radius of the circle, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares.

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+5x-3y-8 & =0 \\ ({x}^{2}+5x)+({y}^{2}-3y) & =8 \\ ({x}^{2}+2\cdot \frac{5}{2}x+{(\frac{5}{2})}^{2})+({y}^{2}-2\cdot \frac{3}{2}y+{(\frac{3}{2})}^{2}) & =8+{(\frac{5}{2})}^{2}+{(\frac{3}{2})}^{2} \\ ({x}^{2}+2\cdot \frac{5}{2}x+{(\frac{5}{2})}^{2})+({y}^{2}-2\cdot \frac{3}{2}y+{(\frac{3}{2})}^{2}) & =\frac{33}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can factor the perfect squares and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{(x+\frac{5}{2})}^{2}+{(y-\frac{3}{2})}^{2} & =\frac{33}{2} \\ {(x+\frac{5}{2})}^{2}+{(y-\frac{3}{2})}^{2} & ={(\sqrt{\frac{33}{2}})}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the circle is centered at $(-\frac{5}{2},\frac{3}{2})$ and its radius is $\sqrt{\frac{33}{2}}.$

questions.problem: Find the center and radius of the circle whose equation is ${x}^{2}+2x+{y}^{2}=55+10y.$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the center and radius of the circle, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares.

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+2x+{y}^{2} & =55+10y \\ ({x}^{2}+2x)+({y}^{2}-10y) & =55 \\ ({x}^{2}+2\cdot x+{1}^{2})+({y}^{2}-2\cdot 5y+{5}^{2}) & =55+{1}^{2}+{5}^{2} \\ ({x}^{2}+2\cdot x+{1}^{2})+({y}^{2}-2\cdot 5y+{5}^{2}) & =81\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can factor the perfect squares and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+1)^{2}+(y-5)^{2} & ={9}^{2} \\ (x-(-1))^{2}+(y-5)^{2} & ={9}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the circle is centered at $(-1,5)$ and its radius is $9.$

questions.problem: Find the center and radius of the circle whose equation is ${x}^{2}-24x+{y}^{2}+6y=-137.$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the center and radius of the circle, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares.

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-24x+{y}^{2}+6y & =-137 \\ ({x}^{2}-24x)+({y}^{2}+6y) & =-137 \\ ({x}^{2}-2\cdot 12x+{12}^{2})+({y}^{2}+2\cdot 3y+{3}^{2}) & =-137+{12}^{2}+{3}^{2} \\ ({x}^{2}-2\cdot 12x+{12}^{2})+({y}^{2}+2\cdot 3y+{3}^{2}) & =16\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can factor the perfect squares and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-12)^{2}+(y+3)^{2} & ={4}^{2} \\ (x-12)^{2}+(y-(-3))^{2} & ={4}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the circle is centered at $(12,-3)$ and its radius is $4.$
